selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main problem the speaker points out in the nafs at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It loves attention, praise, and feeling important.

questions.question: What does the passage say would have to be true for the nafs to have a right to boast?
questions.answer: It would have to be the real producer of the blessings it carries.

questions.question: Why are those examples not meant to prove the nafs is great?
questions.answer: Because they challenge the idea that visible means deserve full credit.

questions.question: What duty is given instead of taking pride in good deeds?
questions.answer: Offering thanks to Allah.

questions.question: What is the proper reaction to personal achievements according to the passage?
questions.answer: Gratitude, not boasting.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the nafs with nature?
questions.answer: It says both have a similar created role as receivers, not independent agents.

questions.question: Why were the nafs and nature created as coverings or veils?
questions.answer: So things whose beauty is not obvious would be linked to them, while Allah is known to be free of defect.

questions.question: What serious spiritual error happens when the nafs forgets its true role?
questions.answer: It behaves as if it shares in the Creator’s work.

questions.question: Why should a person not think being selected to display good works proves personal worth?
questions.answer: Because the selection can come from greater need, not from greater merit.

questions.question: What should Muslim students learn from this when they do well in school or service?
questions.answer: They should thank Allah, stay humble, and not act as if success came only from themselves.

questions.question: What warning from the opening verse matches the lesson of this passage?
questions.answer: People should not feel secure when they enjoy praise for things that are not truly theirs.

questions.question: What false loves of the nafs are named near the start?
questions.answer: Love of status, fame, and praise.

questions.question: Why does the passage say that claim fails in reality?
questions.answer: Because the nafs misuses its will and spoils what it receives.

questions.question: What does thanklessness do to those blessings?
questions.answer: It removes their value in the sight of proper servanthood.

questions.question: What should replace wanting praise from people?
questions.answer: Repentance and asking Allah to forgive.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the nafs in a person and nature in the world?
questions.answer: Both are described as receivers, not real makers.

questions.question: What is the proper understanding of its role in relation to evil?
questions.answer: Evil is connected to it because of its failure and misuse.

questions.question: According to the passage, what may be the real reason a person receives many gifts?
questions.answer: Greater need and poverty before Allah.

questions.question: How can this passage help a student stay sincere when receiving praise from others?
questions.answer: It reminds him that all good is from Allah and that praise should lead to shukr, not arrogance.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to directly throughout most of this passage?
questions.answer: The speaker’s own nafs.

questions.question: What role do the examples from plants play in the argument?
questions.answer: They give a simple picture showing that means are not the true source.

questions.question: Why is the nafs less excusable than a seed or branch?
questions.answer: Because it has choice and responsibility.

questions.question: What should replace pride in one’s actions?
questions.answer: Thankfulness to Allah.

questions.question: What should replace the wish for praise?
questions.answer: Repentance and asking Allah for forgiveness.

title: Title and 1 Point Discipline and Gratitude Lesson for the Commanding Self
